summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex bariatric surgical history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by marginal ulcers and later open reversal) and chronic abdominal pain was admitted with epigastric pain, nausea/vomiting, and profuse diarrhea after difficulty keeping down home GI medications. CT abdomen/pelvis showed a gastro-gastric fistula without obstruction or infectious process; bariatric surgery felt there was no acute surgical issue and GI did not recommend urgent endoscopy. Stool testing was positive for C. difficile, and she was started on oral vancomycin with improvement in diarrhea and ability to tolerate diet by discharge. Pain was managed with resumption of acid-suppression/sucralfate and non-opioid measures with a short course of PRN oxycodone for the acute flare and planned follow-up with chronic pain clinic; asymptomatic bacteriuria with mixed flora was not treated.
problems: Fistula of stomach and duodenum (gastro-gastric fistula on CT)
Chronic abdominal pain (suspected postoperative visceral hyperalgesia)
Medication nonadherence due to poor PO tolerance/missed GI meds
